newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks end weaker, talk of offer for UAP.
newsitem.headline: French stocks end weaker, talk of offer for UAP.

text.p: French stocks finished marginally weaker, barely above day lows, after five days on the rise, with carmaker Renault marking the biggest loss after predicting that it could end the year in the red.
Traders reported a late block trade of 250,000 shares in insurer UAP and market talk of an offer for the group with Axa as predator. Axa denied the market rumour.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index closed down 4.06 points or 0.2 percent at 2,038.06, while the CAC-40 futures contract ended off 2.0 points at 2045.0 from Tuesday's close.
Volume was a solid 4.68 billion francs.

* Union des Assurances de Paris (UAP) up 3.3 francs, or 3.29 percent, at 103.5. Traders said 250,000 shares changed hands at 105.30 francs per share in a block trade at 1450 GMT amid market talk of a public offer with rival Axa as predator.
Takeover talks has stalked UAP since the start of the year due to the weakness of its shares, which were sold to small investors at 152 francs when firm was privatised in 1994.
*Axa 1.6 francs, or 0.56 percent, lower at 283.9 francs. Spokeswoman responds: "Axa denies the rumours, according to which it is making a public offer for UAP."
* Renault shares end down 5.04 percent at 113 francs but off day's low. Carmaker forecast full-year loss after disappointing first-half results released on Tuesday.
S&P says it puts long-term debt of Renault Credit International and subsidiaries on credit watch with negative implications.
* PSA Peugeot Citroen was also weaker in sympathy, off 10 francs at 559, or down 1.76 percent but off low of 553.
* The COB stockmarket regulator announced early on Wednesday a probe into information concerning possible buyout by investment company CGIP of Cerus holding company and car parts maker Valeo.

CGIP ends down 27 francs or 2.27 percent at 1,162. It has denied plans to launch takeover bid for Cerus but newspaper Les Echos quoted CGIP chairman Ernest-Antoine Seilliere as confirming interest in 28 percent of Valeo which Cerus holds.
Les Echos says matter could be resolved in early October following board meetings of various companies involved.
Valeo up 4.0 francs or 0.14 percent at 280 francs. Cerus down 6.0 francs or 4.51 percent at 127.0 francs.

*Electrical retailer Legrand 4.33 percent higher. It warned analysts it did not expect any "significant increase" in 1996 profits after reporting first-half net profit fell 3.2 percent to 453 million francs. But it said earlier this week results trend should be favourable for company in coming years.

* Media group Pathe higher after better-than-expected first half results prompt analysts to raise 1996 forecasts. Analysts said the first-half figures were particularly good for film production and distribution.
